extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, indexers, and publishers (production staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards from a comprehensive publishing/style manual (Chicago Manual–style) covering punctuation, capitalization, citations, typography, illustrations, electronic-publication handling, and production practices for books, journals, and related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: usage of and / ampersand / conjunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using 'and' and ampersand (&) in text, titles, lists, publisher names, authors/editors in citations, sentences beginning with conjunctions, and effects on verb number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers when to use ampersand vs. 'and' (e.g., publishers’ names, source citations), interaction with serial commas, punctuation with conjunctions, use as subordinating conjunction, slash instead of 'and', 'and/or' usage, and special cases like 'and other stories' and 'and so forth'. See cross-references to ampersands and conjunctions (entries: 6.21, 14.76, 5.205, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: angle brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of angle brackets for callouts, generic markup, special characters, URLs/emails, mathematical expressions, and XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify contexts where angle brackets are appropriate (callouts, markup, less-than/greater-than, mathematical dirac notation) and reference font and punctuation interactions; see guidance on XML and URLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: annotations and annotated bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat annotations, including keyed annotations to line/page numbers and annotated bibliographies formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotations as copyrightable; keyed annotations in figs.; annotations in PDF files. Annotated bibliographies formatting referenced (fig. 14.10). See also notes and source citations guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: anonymity of research subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial/ethical requirement to protect anonymity of research subjects in publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointed guidance on anonymizing research-subject information (entry 13.49). Relevance to permissions, attribution, and bias-free language.

rubrics_metrics.name: anonymous works (copyright & citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of anonymous works for copyright and how to cite works with anonymous or pseudonymous authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers copyright of anonymous works, source-citation forms for anonymous works, use of 'Anonymous' and 'Anon.' in citations, and cross-references to notes/bibliography and author-date systems (14.79, 15.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: apostrophes (use and marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for apostrophe usage: possessives, plurals, contractions, editorial marking, language-specific rules, and interactions with other punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on marking on manuscript/proofs, electronic-file cleanup, uses in plurals and possessives (with many subcases: attributive nouns, compounds, joint possessives, etc.), distinction from prime symbol and single closing quotation mark, inappropriate uses, and language-specific rules for multiple languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: appendixes (format, numbering, placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for appendices/appendixes: numbering, placement in book, formatting, submission, and indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes appendixes as electronic supplementary data, inclusion of chronologies, discographies, glossaries as appendices, numbering of figures/tables in appendices, parenthetical references to appendixes, running heads, multiple appendices, and submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: appositives (definition and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of appositive constructions and punctuation rules (commas, subordinate conjunctions, titles/offices as appositives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains commas with appositives, appositives and pronouns, relation to serial commas, and grammatical placement for place-names and titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: apps (electronic publications and apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on apps as a publication format: functional features, indexing, markup, multimedia, navigation, PDF format, proofing/testing, and citation format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers apps' required features for reading electronic publications, metadata, site map, multimedia content and video games as apps, submission and production testing, and how to cite apps in source citations (14.137, 14.159, 14.189, 14.268).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arabic language and script guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Language-specific guidance for Arabic: capitalization (where relevant), special characters, spelling, word division, and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References sections on Arabic language usage, article and name treatment, and special-character tables; includes resources and indexing references (11.76–81).

rubrics_metrics.name: arabic numerals (use and contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for where to use arabic numerals vs. roman numerals, usage in addresses/building numbers, page and volume numbering, parts of books, ranges, and in source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on ranges (inclusive), sequencing (vs. roman numerals), table columns, spacecraft numbers, parts of books and poems, and many citation-specific rules for journals, classical works, scriptural references, and multivolume works.

rubrics_metrics.name: archival practices and backup copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for archival practices and maintaining backup copies of manuscripts and citation data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers archival practices as part of production, backup copies of manuscripts and electronic files (responsibility of authors), and relation to citation-data backups (14.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: articles (definite and indefinite) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using 'a', 'an', and 'the' including omission, language-specific treatments, capitalization in titles, indexing, and syntactic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions, appropriate use, omission in titles/headlines, handling in various languages (Arabic), behavior in index alphabetizing and subentries, and special cases (collective nouns, headline-style capitalization).

rubrics_metrics.name: artwork (credit, submission, copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for artwork: inventory, submission guidelines, credit lines, cropping/scaling, copyright issues, and source citations for artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers commissioned artwork, continuous-tone images, covers and jackets, creators' names and indexing, redrawing by publisher, scans, original dimensions, source citations for images, proofing, submission, and permissions/fees for artwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: attribution and fair-use principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance and limits of attribution in relation to copyright and fair-use doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how attribution relates to fair use, when attribution is necessary or unnecessary, and cross-references to illustration credits, source and text citations, and permissions guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: attributive adjectives and nouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammatical guidance distinguishing attributive adjectives and nouns and their punctuation/usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on use of attributive nouns and adjectives, including related references to capitalization and hyphenation where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: audiobooks and audio-rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of audiobooks and related audio rights: citation, rights management, and relation to multimedia content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates where audiobooks and audio rights are covered and their relationship to multimedia and sound-recording treatments and permissions (1.75, 14.264, 4.64).

rubrics_metrics.name: author-date reference system
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and formatting for the author-date reference system: author name forms, publication dates, page locators, examples, and discipline variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers basic format (fig. 15.1), handling of more than three authors, editors in place of authors, cross-checking, indexing interactions, use in journals, handling of forthcoming or 'no date' items, social media/webpage treatments, and differences vs. notes-and-bibliography system.

rubrics_metrics.name: author queries (marking and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for author queries during editing: marking, placement, style, and topics for queries (ambiguity, bias-free language, cross-references, quotations, source citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes placement in margins, comment style, sticky notes, electronic insertion, examples (fig. 2.4), and how queries interact with fact-checking and tracking changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: authors' responsibilities in production
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities of authors in the publication process (proofreading, backups, permissions, communication with editors, metadata, and royalties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers approval before editing, sending edited manuscripts, proofing, list of previous publications on copyright page, indexing roles, proof corrections (AAs), warranties, translations, websites, and responsibility for permissions and royalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: authors' names in citations (formats and special cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format authors' names in different citation systems, including ordering, initials vs. full names, repeated names, pseudonyms, organizations as authors, and special rules for multiple works and same-year publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for author-date and notes-and-bibliography systems, examples, cross-references to indexing, 3-em dash usage for repeated names, handling of anonymous works, editors-as-authors, mononyms, and various language-specific norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: back matter (components and placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard components of back matter (acknowledgments, appendixes, bibliography/reference list, biographical notes, chronologies, colophons, editor's notes, endnotes, glossaries, illustration credits, indexes) and formatting/pagination guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes electronic-publication considerations, indexing of back-matter material, placement in book, pagination, running heads, presence in journals, and production-checklist references.

rubrics_metrics.name: backup copies (production requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement and practice of maintaining backup copies of manuscript files and citation data throughout production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies backup of electronic files and paper-only manuscripts, archival practices, responsibility (authors/production), and cross-reference to citation-data backups.

rubrics_metrics.name: bias-free language
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and alternatives for bias-free language, with emphasis on avoiding gender bias and other biases in editorial practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes alternatives, editor attention to bias-free language, guidance for necessary gender-specific language, noun forms, sex-specific labels, and references to related editorial responsibilities and author queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bible and biblical citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of biblical materials: abbreviations, chapter/verse citation format, capitalization, versions, and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on abbreviations in biblical citations, punctuation, chapter and verse formatting (14.239), handling versions and sections, capitalization rules, language-specific notes (Hebrew), and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: bibliographies (format, alphabetization, inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for bibliographies: alphabetizing (letter-by-letter vs word-by-word), format and hanging indentation, authors' name ordering, headnotes, types (annotated, selected, discographies), inclusion criteria, and indexing interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers readability considerations, examples (figs. 14.8–11), headnotes/sections, editing/checking bibliographies, notes vs reference lists differences, submission guidelines, and special cases (multiauthor volumes, chronological ordering).

rubrics_metrics.name: block quotations (formatting and permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for block quotations: indentation, capitalization, punctuation (colons, ellipses, periods, quotation marks), converting to run-in, notes within, paragraphs, and permissions for long quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes manuscript preparation guidelines, generic markup, indenting, treatment of quotations from non-English materials, note references within blocks, handling of poetry quotations, proofreading, and permissions requirements (4.95, 13.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: blogs and blog posts (citation and text treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite blogs and blog posts and how to treat them in text (author-date, source-citation forms, and handling in references and text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines blog posts, shows citation examples and variations (14.205–208, 15.51), guidance for treatment in running text or titles (8.192), and cross-references to social media and URLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: brackets (use and punctuation interactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage of brackets (square, angle, braces) for editorial interpolations, mathematical expressions, music dynamics, phonetics, URLs, and citation contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies angle bracket uses, Dirac bracket notation, font considerations, interplay with commas/periods/quotation marks, use with sic, and when to use brackets for translated text or editorial clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: boldface (uses and marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate uses of boldface (emphasis, computer terminology, musical dynamics, highlighting key terms) and guidance for marking bold in manuscripts/proofs and its interaction with punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for marking bold in manuscripts and proofs, proofreading considerations, use in indexes and mathematical copy, and examples of contexts where bold is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: book production (divisions, pagination, metadata, parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for book structure and production: front/back matter, pagination conventions, parts/chapters, running heads, page-count definitions, metadata, simultaneous print/electronic publishing, errata, interactive features, and signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers abstracting for books, page and signature definitions, pagination style for poetry and chapters, metadata for electronic formats, e-books and multiple formats citation rules, production schedule references, and submission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: callouts (illustration/table references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format and handling of callouts for illustrations and tables, including definition, numbering, placement, markup, and cross-references to text references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on markup, working numbers, placement relative to features, whether to spell out 'figure' or 'table' in callouts, cross-checking, and checking against feature placement (2.26, 3.8, 3.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: capitalization (general rules and contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for capitalization across contexts: names, titles, organizations, common nouns, languages, glossaries, indexes, emphasis, and cross-language exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes capitalization in lists, illustration labels, indexes (main head/subentry), editorial notes, ellipses, treatment for groups (ethnic, generational), historical/cultural terminology, scientific/technical terms, and sparing 'down style'; references language-specific sections and editorial permissions for changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: caps and small caps formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use full-size caps vs small caps, and how to mark/format caps in indexes, legal citations, mathematical copy, and drama speaker names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that full-size caps are preferred to small caps for emphasis in many contexts; includes usage in indexes, legal-style citations, mathematical copy, and for speaker names in drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: captions (format and accessibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for captions for figures and tables: definition, capitalization, credit lines, accessibility considerations, examples for charts and illustrations, and handling of illustrations with parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers caption capitalization, inclusion of illustration credits, marking electronic supplementary data in captions, accessibility concerns, examples of caption formats (figs.), and handling of multipart illustrations and journal cover captions.
